note: The closest match to the stated ICP in this batch and arguably in the corpus, because he satisfies the criterion the ICP names most explicitly. The stated definition says prospects 'own their own business, or they're a physician, something along those lines' — he is a physician who has just completed residency, and also a serving Air Force officer. Income holds on the criterion as written: a newly qualified attending physician starting a new post makes good money, and his objection is a preference rather than an incapacity — 'That would be more than what I'd want to spend', which is a ceiling he chose, not one imposed on him. Neglected health is textbook and in his own words: 'I just finished medical residency, so I was just super stressed, couldn't really work out.' Good to great holds because he is not being rescued — he has already held 155 lb under a previous coach and wants 162 lb back plus slow muscle gain. Not deconditioned holds on both halves of the exclusion: roughly 23 lb above his own target rather than fifty, and emphatically not gym-averse, having trained almost daily three years ago and currently running and doing calisthenics for a service fitness test. The finding worth carrying to the rollup is not the fit but what happened to it. The one prospect in this batch who matches every stated criterion is the one who was never given a price, never asked a commitment question, never taken through a consequence frame and never subjected to a money play. If the ICP is meant to identify who the process should be run hardest on, this call is evidence the two are not connected.
